claim: Protein phosphorylation is a reversible post-translation modification essential in cell signaling.
source: Protein phosphorylation is a reversible post-translation modification essential in cell signaling.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about protein phosphorylation.

claim: PP2A regulatory subunit B55α recruits p107, a pRB-related tumor suppressor and B55α substrate.
source: Here, we show how the PP2A regulatory subunit B55α recruits p107, a pRB-related tumor suppressor and B55α substrate.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on molecular and cellular approaches described in the manuscript.

claim: A conserved region 1 (R1, residues 615–626) encompasses the strongest p107 binding site for B55α.
source: Using molecular and cellular approaches, we identified a conserved region 1 (R1, residues 615–626) encompassing the strongest p107 binding site.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from molecular and cellular approaches presented in the study.

claim: An 'HxRVxxV619-625' short linear motif (SLiM) in p107 is necessary for B55α binding and dephosphorylation of the proximal pSer-615 in vitro and in cells.
source: This enabled us to identify an 'HxRVxxV619-625' short linear motif (SLiM) in p107 as necessary for B55α binding and dephosphorylation of the proximal pSer-615 in vitro and in cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data from in vitro and cellular assays.

claim: Numerous B55α/PP2A substrates, including TAU, contain a related SLiM C-terminal from a proximal phosphosite, 'p[ST]-P-x(4,10)-[RK]-V-x-x-[VI]-R.'
source: Numerous B55α/PP2A substrates, including TAU, contain a related SLiM C-terminal from a proximal phosphosite, 'p[ST]-P-x(4,10)-[RK]-V-x-x-[VI]-R.'
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and comparison of multiple B55α substrates.

claim: Mutation of conserved SLiM residues in TAU dramatically inhibits dephosphorylation by PP2A/B55α.
source: Mutation of conserved SLiM residues in TAU dramatically inhibits dephosphorylation by PP2A/B55α, validating its generality.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from dephosphorylation assays with TAU mutants.

claim: A third of all cellular proteins are phosphorylated.
source: It is estimated that a third of all cellular proteins are phosphorylated (Ficarro et al., 2002)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ficarro et al., 2002.

claim: More than 98% of phosphorylation events occur on serine and threonine residues.
source: with more than 98% of those phosphorylation events occurring on serine and threonine residues (Olsen et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Olsen et al., 2006.

claim: PP1 and PP2A account for more than 90% of the total phosphatase activity in eukaryotic cells.
source: with protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) and protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A) accounting for more than 90% of the total phosphatase activity (Moorhead et al., 2007; Virshup and Shenolikar, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Moorhead et al., 2007 and Virshup and Shenolikar, 2009.

claim: PP1 substrate recognition involves defined short linear motifs (SLiMs) including RVxF, ΦΦ, and SILK.
source: Within the PPP family, the molecular details of substrate recognition have been best studied for PP1 and calcineurin (or PP2B), and involve the recognition of defined short linear motifs (SLiMs) including RVxF,ΦΦ (where Φrefers to a hydrophobic residue), SILK, among others for PP1 (Choy et al., 2014; Kumar et al., 2018)
evidence: This is supported by citations to Choy et al., 2014 and Kumar et al., 2018.

claim: Calcineurin (PP2B) substrate recognition involves LxVP and PxIxIT motifs.
source: and LxVP and PxIxIT for PP2B.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about calcineurin substrate recognition.

claim: PP2A makes up close to 1% of total cellular protein in some tissue types.
source: PP2A is a highly conserved Ser/Thr protein phosphatase that makes up close to 1% of total cellular protein in some tissue types, making it one of the most abundant enzymes (Fowle et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fowle et al., 2019.

claim: PP2A can exist as a heterodimeric 'core enzyme' consisting of a scaffold (A) subunit and a catalytic (C) subunit.
source: As a multimeric protein, PP2A can exist as a heterodimeric 'core enzyme,' consisting of a scaffold (A) subunit and a catalytic (C) subunit
evidence: This is established knowledge about PP2A structure.

claim: PP2A can exist as a heterotrimeric holoenzyme in which the core dimer complexes with a B subunit.
source: or a heterotrimeric holoenzyme, in which the core dimer complexes with a B subunit (reviewed in Shi, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Shi, 2009.

claim: The B subunit of PP2A can be subdivided into one of four major families (B55, B56, B72, and B93).
source: The B subunit of PP2A can be subdivided into one of four major families (B55, B56, B72, and B93), each consisting of 2–5 isoforms and numerous splice variants.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PP2A B subunit classification.

claim: The B subunits are thought to be the key determinant of substrate specificity for the PP2A complex.
source: Apart from its role in subcellular localization, the B subunits are thought to be the key determinant of substrate specificity for the PP2A complex (reviewed in Fowle et al., 2019; Kurimchak and Graña, 2012; Virshup and Shenolikar, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Fowle et al., 2019; Kurimchak and Graña, 2012; Virshup and Shenolikar, 2009.

claim: A PP2A substrate SLiM (LxxIxE) has been identified for the B56 family of PP2A regulatory subunits.
source: Indeed, a PP2A substrate SLiM (LxxIxE) has recently been identified for the B56 family of PP2A regulatory subunits, which form a HEAT repeat fold.
evidence: This is stated as a recent finding about B56 substrate recognition.

claim: The binding affinity of LxxIxE can be modulated by phosphorylation, with phosphorylation leading to tighter binding.
source: The binding affinity of LxxIxE can be modulated by phosphorylation (phosphorylation leads to tighter binding)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the B56 SLiM.

claim: The LxxIxE motif binds in a binding pocket between HEAT repeats 3 and 4 of B56.
source: and it binds in a binding pocket between HEAT repeats 3 and 4.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the B56 SLiM binding site.

claim: Conserved, dynamic charged:charged interactions modulate substrate specificity for B56.
source: Furthermore, it was recently shown that additional factors including conserved, dynamic charged:charged interaction modulate substrate specificity for B56 (Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2020.

claim: B55α is ubiquitously expressed and the most abundant regulatory subunit of PP2A.
source: B55α (four isoforms, α, β, ɣ, δ; our work focuses on the α-isoform of B55) is ubiquitously expressed and the most abundant regulatory subunit of PP2A (Kim et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2014 and Wang et al., 2015.

claim: All known PP2A/B55α-dependent substrates have key functions in cell division, differentiation, and survival.
source: Critically, all known PP2A/B55α-dependent substrates have key functions in cell division, differentiation, and survival, and are found to be dysregulated in cancer and Alzheimer's disease (reviewed in Fowle et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Fowle et al., 2019.

claim: It was proposed that the large negatively charged patch on B55α recruits Lys-rich domains of TAU.
source: Specifically, it was proposed the large negatively charged patch on B55α recruits Lys-rich domains of TAU (Xu et al., 2008)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Xu et al., 2008.

claim: Other substrates must use different molecular recognition motifs than the negatively charged patch on B55α.
source: only to be shown that other substrates must use different molecular recognition motifs (Jayadeva et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jayadeva et al., 2010.

claim: Proteomics data suggested that B55α preferred substrates that are phosphorylated by Ser/Thr-Pro directed kinases.
source: Recently, proteomics data suggested that B55α preferred substrates that are phosphorylated by Ser/Thr-Pro directed kinases (Cundell et al., 2016; Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Cundell et al., 2016 and Zhao et al., 2019.

claim: No substrate recruitment mechanism has been identified for B55α prior to this study.
source: However, no substrate recruitment mechanism has been identified for B55α
evidence: This is stated as a gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: p107 is a pRB-related tumor suppressor with key regulatory roles in the cell cycle.
source: p107 is a pRB-related tumor suppressor with key regulatory roles in the cell cycle (reviewed in Kurimchak and Graña, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kurimchak and Graña, 2015.

claim: The p107 'spacer' region (p107 residues 585–780) is sufficient for PP2A/B55α binding.
source: We have previously shown that the p107 'spacer' region (p107 residues 585–780, which link the retinoblastoma conserved regions A and B) is sufficient for PP2A/B55α binding (Jayadeva et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Jayadeva et al., 2010.

claim: The p107 linker region is intrinsically disordered according to IUPred2a bioinformatics analysis.
source: IUPred2a bioinformatics analysis (Mészáros et al., 2018) shows that this linker region is intrinsically disordered (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is based on bioinformatics analysis using IUPred2a and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Aligning the intrinsically disordered p107 linker region from 60 different species enabled the identification of three highly conserved regions (termed R1, R2, and R3).
source: Aligning the intrinsically disordered p107 linker region from 60 different species enabled the identification of three highly conserved regions (termed R1, R2, and R3) (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The conservation of R1 and R2 extended to a conserved family member p130 (RBL2).
source: Indeed, the conservation of R1 and R2 extended to a conserved family member p130 (RBL2) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Within the spacer, there are three potential CDK kinase phosphorylation sites (p107 S615, S640, and S650).
source: Within the spacer, there are also three potential CDK kinase phosphorylation sites (p107 S615, S640, and S650).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and knowledge of CDK phosphorylation motifs.

claim: A mutant lacking residues C-terminal of R2 binds B55α similarly to the full construct.
source: Figure 1D shows that a mutant lacking residues C-terminal of R2 binds B55α similarly to the full construct, indicating that residues C-terminal to the R2 domain are dispensable for B55α binding.
evidence: This is based on GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: R1 alone can bind B55α, although to a slightly lesser extent than R1/R2.
source: R1 alone can bind B55α, although to a slightly lesser extent than R1/R2 (lane 3)
evidence: This is based on GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Mutants lacking regions containing R1 do not bind B55α.
source: while mutants lacking regions containing R1 do not bind B55α (lanes 6 and 7).
evidence: This is based on GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: R1 is the key B55α binding region and R2 enhances the interaction, but without R1 cannot recruit B55α alone.
source: Additional experiments highlighted that R1 is the key B55α binding region and that R2 enhances the interaction, but without R1 cannot recruit B55α alone (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is based on GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Binding of p107 to CDK2 strictly depends on the presence of R2.
source: Conversely, binding of p107 to CDK2 (or cyclin A, not shown) strictly depends on the presence of R2 (lanes 2, 4, 5, and 6), which includes an RxL motif necessary for cyclin A/CDK2 binding (Adams et al., 1996; Chen et al., 1996).
evidence: This is based on GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 1D and supported by citations to Adams et al., 1996 and Chen et al., 1996.

claim: Positive residues in R1 and R2, but not the connecting s2 'linker,' led to a reduction in binding to B55α.
source: As shown in Figure 1D, positive residues in R1 and R2, but not the connecting s2 'linker,' led to a reduction in binding to B55α.
evidence: This is based on GST pull-down assay data with p107 mutants shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Mutation of the cyclin A binding site in R2 (659KRRL-AAAA and 660RRL-AAA mutations to Ala) reduced binding to B55α.
source: Mutation of the cyclin A binding site in R2 (659KRRL-AAAA and 660RRL-AAA mutations to Ala), which also contains positive residues, also reduced binding (data not shown).
evidence: This is based on experimental data not shown in the manuscript.

claim: Positively charged residues participate in binding to B55α.
source: Thus, positively charged residues participate in binding to B55α.
evidence: This is inferred from the mutagenesis data showing that mutation of positive residues reduces binding.

claim: The 2D [1H,15N] HSQC spectrum of 15N-labeled p107 (residues M612-S687) shows all hallmarks of an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP).
source: The 2D [1H,15N] HSQC spectrum of 15N-labeled p107 (residues M612-S687, which include R1, R2, and R3) shows all hallmarks of an intrinsically disordered protein (IDP), with a highly limited proton chemical shift dispersion due to the lack of a hydrogen bond network in secondary structure elements.
evidence: This is based on NMR spectroscopy data.

claim: NMR data experimentally validates the bioinformatics prediction that p107 is intrinsically disordered.
source: This experimentally validates the bioinformatics data.
evidence: This is inferred from the agreement between NMR data and bioinformatics predictions.

claim: Cross-peaks corresponding to p107 residues M614-E624 were most significantly broadened upon binding to B55α.
source: Upon completion of the sequence-specific backbone assignment of p107M612-S687, we identified that cross-peaks corresponding to p107 residues M614-E624 were most significantly broadened upon binding to B55α (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is based on NMR spectroscopy data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: p107 residues M614-E624 form the core of R1.
source: Consistent with the mutation data, these residues form the core of R1.
evidence: This is inferred from the NMR data and sequence analysis.

claim: Residues within the linker region and R2 also showed peak intensity attenuations, consistent with additional weaker interactions in R2 contributing and enhancing the interaction of R1.
source: Furthermore, residues within the linker region and R2 also showed peak intensity attenuations, consistent with additional weaker interactions in R2 contributing and enhancing the interaction of R1.
evidence: This is based on NMR spectroscopy data.

claim: The p107 R1 region mediates key contacts with B55α.
source: Taken together, the NMR data reinforce that the p107 R1 region mediates key contacts with B55α.
evidence: This is inferred from the NMR data showing peak broadening in R1 upon B55α binding.

claim: The most highly conserved residues in B55α cluster at the top of the β-propeller and a fraction of them form a highly negatively charged patch.
source: The most highly conserved residues cluster at the top of the β-propeller and a fraction of them form a highly negatively charged patch (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on conservation analysis and electrostatic surface analysis shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: There is a prominent groove on the surface of B55α blade 4 that might function as a potential guide for substrates to reach the catalytic site of PP2A/C.
source: Based on this analysis and the observation of a prominent groove on the surface of B55α blade 4 (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1) that might function as a potential guide for substrates to reach the catalytic site of PP2A/C
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and speculation about function.

claim: All B55α residues tested except E27 are conserved in the other three members of the B55 family.
source: All these residues except E27, which lies in a protein segment not present in B55γ, are conserved in the other three members of the B55 family.
evidence: This is based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: B55α D197K and L225A variants showed the most profound impact on the recruitment of all three substrates (p107, pRB, and KSR1) when directly compared to wildtype B55α.
source: B55α D197K and L225A variants showed the most profound impact on the recruitment of all three substrates when directly compared to wildtype B55α.
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: Other B55α mutants showed varying effects on binding depending on the substrate.
source: Other B55α mutants showed varying effects on binding depending on the substrate, as illustrated by B55α V228A affecting only p107 binding while B55α H179A affected p107 and KSR1 but not pRB binding (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: B55α D197K was the only variant that had a minor effect on PP2A/A and PP2A/C recruitment.
source: B55α D197K was the only variant that had a minor effect on PP2A/A and PP2A/C recruitment (Figure 2D, left panel).
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: All substrates use the highly conserved top and groove of B55α for their interaction.
source: Taken together, while all substrates use the highly conserved top and groove of B55α for their interaction, our data demonstrate the contribution of distinct residues on the B55α surface for binding to different substrates (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is inferred from the mutagenesis data showing that different substrates require different B55α residues.

claim: The two B55α residues required by the three substrates tested, D197K and L225A, are located on the B55α blade 4, which directly points towards the active site of PP2A/C.
source: The two B55α residues required by the three substrates tested, D197K and L225A, are located on the B55α blade 4, which directly points towards the active site of PP2A/C.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and mutagenesis data.

claim: PP2A/B55α is known to counteract phosphorylation by CDK kinases during mitosis.
source: PP2A/B55α is known to counteract phosphorylation by CDK kinases during mitosis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: p107M612-S687 contains three SP sites (S615, S640, and S650) that can be phosphorylated in cells.
source: p107M612-S687 contains three SP sites (S615, S640, and S650, Figure 1C) that can be phosphorylated in cells (Hornbeck et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hornbeck et al., 2015.

claim: Recombinant cyclin A/CDK2 and γ-32P-ATP showed robust in vitro phosphorylation of p107.
source: Using recombinant cyclin A/CDK2 and γ-32P-ATP, we observed robust in vitro phosphorylation of p107.
evidence: This is based on in vitro kinase assay data.

claim: At least two different sites on p107 are phosphorylated by cyclin A/CDK2.
source: Our data suggested that at least two different sites are phosphorylated (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, top).
evidence: This is based on in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: MS identified pS615 and pS640 in CDK2-phosphorylated p107.
source: MS identified pS615 and pS640 in CDK2-phosphorylated p107
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data.

claim: MS showed a significant reduction of pS615 and pS640 phosphorylation upon incubation with PP2A/B55α.
source: and a significant reduction of pS615 and pS640 phosphorylation upon incubation with PP2A/B55α (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: S650 phosphorylation was not identified by MS, likely due to the close proximity of S650 to the RXL658-660 motif that mediates cyclin A/CDK2 binding to p107.
source: Interestingly, S650 phosphorylation was not identified, likely due to the close proximity of S650 to the RXL658-660 motif that mediates cyclin A/CDK2 binding to p107.
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data and speculation about the reason for not detecting S650 phosphorylation.

claim: Purified PP2A/B55α dephosphorylates p107 in a time-dependent manner.
source: To further analyze PP2A/B55α-mediated dephosphorylation, we purified recombinant PP2A/B55α (Figure 3A, right panel; Zhao et al., 2019) and used this functional holoenzyme to analyze time-dependent dephosphorylation of p107M612-S687 (Figure 3A, left panel)
evidence: This is based on in vitro dephosphorylation assay data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: PP2A/B55α-mediated dephosphorylation of p107 is inhibited by 10 nM of the PP2A/C-specific inhibitor okadaic acid.
source: which is inhibited by 10 nM of the PP2A/C-specific inhibitor okadaic acid.
evidence: This is based on in vitro dephosphorylation assay data with okadaic acid.

claim: Reduced dephosphorylation of p107 was detected for the binding-deficient p107 R1 [R621A/K623A] variant when compared to wt-p107.
source: As expected, reduced dephosphorylation of p107 was detected for the binding-deficient p107 R1 [R621A/K623A] variant when compared to wt-p107, confirming our newly identified substrate binding residues (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on in vitro dephosphorylation assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Dephosphorylation was further reduced for the p107-R1-R2 variant (R1 [R621A/K623A]-R2 [K657A/R659A]).
source: Dephosphorylation was further reduced for the p107-R1-R2 variant (R1 [R621A/K623A]-R2 [K657A/R659A]) (Figure 4A), correlating well with the NMR-based binding affinities.
evidence: This is based on in vitro dephosphorylation assay data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Dephosphorylation of p107 was significantly reduced when PP2A/B55α incubated with the R1 peptide was used for dephosphorylation studies.
source: As expected, dephosphorylation of p107 was significantly reduced when PP2A/B55α incubated with the R1 peptide was used for dephosphorylation studies (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is based on competitive peptide dephosphorylation assay data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: Repeating the competitive peptide experiment using a binding-deficient peptide (either R1 R621A or R2) showed dephosphorylation kinetics similar to that of the free PP2A/B55α.
source: Repeating this experiment using a binding-deficient peptide (either R1 R621A or R2) showed dephosphorylation kinetics similar to that of the free PP2A/B55α, suggesting that the mutant peptide bound too weakly to compete for the substrate binding site on PP2A/B55α (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is based on competitive peptide dephosphorylation assay data shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: The R1 peptide was able to compete with a p107 R1R2 construct for B55α binding.
source: This peptide was able to compete with a p107 R1R2 construct.
evidence: This is based on binding competition assay data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Using different peptides, such as R2 or small spacer peptides, did not show a competitive effect on B55α binding.
source: As expected, using different peptides, such as R2 or small spacer peptides, did not show this effect.
evidence: This is based on binding competition assay data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Three triple-mutant peptides were unable to bind PP2A/B55α.
source: Our data clearly showed that three triple-mutant peptides were unable to bind PP2A/B55α (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on binding competition assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The main R1 interaction residues must be within p107 M618-R626.
source: These data showed that the main R1 interaction residues must be within p107 M618-R626.
evidence: This is inferred from the triple-mutant peptide binding data.

claim: p107 residues H619, R621, V622, and V625 are critical for B55α binding.
source: These experiments showed that p107 residues H619, R621, V622, and V625 are critical for B55α binding as R1 peptides with H619A, R621A, V622A, and V625A bound poorly to PP2A/B55α (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, top).
evidence: This is based on binding competition assay data with single Ala substitution peptides shown in Figure 5C.

claim: H619A, R621A, V622A, and V625A dramatically reduce binding to B55α holoenzymes.
source: Moreover, to confirm the requirement of each one of these residues for binding to B55α, we generated point mutants and tested them in binding assays. H619A, R621A, V622A, and V625A dramatically reduce binding to B55α holoenzymes (Figure 5—figure supplement 1, bottom).
evidence: This is based on binding assay data with point mutants shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: A putative SLiM binding motif for p107 with PP2A/B55α is HxRVxxV.
source: These experiments defined a putative SLiM binding motif for p107 – HxRVxxV – with PP2A/B55α.
evidence: This is inferred from the mutagenesis data identifying critical residues.

claim: The mutant phosphopeptides (H619A or R621A) were dephosphorylated by purified PP2A/B55α at a slower rate compared to the wildtype pS615-R1 phosphopeptide.
source: Figure 5D shows that the mutant phosphopeptides were dephosphorylated by purified PP2A/B55α at a slower rate compared to the wildtype pS615-R1 phosphopeptide.
evidence: This is based on Malachite Green Phosphatase Assay data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The p107-based putative HxRVxxV SLiM docks at the mouth of the B55α groove (between blades 3 and 4 of the β-propeller) and the 'SP' site within the active site of the PP2A/C catalytic subunit.
source: Altogether, these binding and enzymatic assay data support a mechanism whereby the p107-based putative HxRVxxV SLiM docks at the mouth of the B55α groove (between blades 3 and 4 of the β-propeller) and the 'SP' site within the active site of the PP2A/C catalytic subunit.
evidence: This is inferred from the binding and dephosphorylation data.

claim: GFP-p107-R1, but not mutant GFP-p107-R1 (H/AxR/AV/AxxV/A variant), immunoprecipitates both endogenous B55α and exogenous Myc-B55α together with PP2A/A.
source: Using co-transfection followed by immunoprecipitation assays, we show that GFP-p107-R1, but not mutant GFP-p107-R1 (H/AxR/AV/AxxV/A variant), immunoprecipitates both endogenous B55α and exogenous Myc-B55α together with PP2A/A (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation assay data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: GFP-R1 did not immunoprecipitate B55α-D197K.
source: As expected, GFP-R1 did not immunoprecipitate B55α-D197K (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation assay data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: R1 is sufficient to form a complex with the PP2A/B55α holoenzyme in cells and this is dependent on B55α D197.
source: This confirms that R1 is sufficient to form a complex with the PP2A/B55α holoenzyme in cells and that this is dependent on B55α D197.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: The specificity of the GFP-p107-R1 fusion protein pulldown was validated by MS, which resulted in the identification of B55α and PP2A/A.
source: The specificity of the GFP-p107-R1 fusion protein pulldown was additionally validated by MS, which resulted in the identification of B55α and PP2A/A (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The p107 R1 domain contains a highly specific SLiM for B55α family members.
source: Therefore, the p107 R1 domain contains a highly specific SLiM for B55α family members.
evidence: This is inferred from the specificity of the interaction shown by MS.

claim: wt B55α expression, but not mt B55α-D197K, leads to reduced phosphorylation of p107 on sites recognized by the CDK substrate antibody.
source: Figure 6C shows that wt B55α expression, but not mt B55α-D197K, leads to reduced phosphorylation of p107 on sites recognized by the CDK substrate antibody, which include p107 S615
evidence: This is based on co-transfection and immunoprecipitation assay data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The binding of WT B55α to the p107 SLiM mutant is drastically diminished.
source: Figure 6D shows that the binding of WT B55α to the p107 SLiM mutant is drastically diminished
evidence: This is based on co-transfection and immunoprecipitation assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The p107 SLiM mutant shows a dramatic increase in the phosphorylation of p107 S615.
source: and this is accompanied by a dramatic increase in the phosphorylation of p107 S615.
evidence: This is based on co-transfection and immunoprecipitation assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: B55αD191K does not bind WT or MT p107, nor affects the phosphorylation state.
source: As expected, B55αD191K does not bind WT or MT p107, nor affects the phosphorylation state.
evidence: This is based on co-transfection and immunoprecipitation assay data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The p107 SLiM is essential to maintain steady-state phosphorylation of at least p107 S615.
source: Therefore, the p107 SLiM is essential to maintain steady-state phosphorylation of at least p107 S615
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing increased S615 phosphorylation in the SLiM mutant.

claim: B55α must be critical for the temporal regulation of at least p107 S615.
source: and thus we can infer that B55α must be critical for the temporal regulation of at least this site.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing B55α-dependent dephosphorylation of S615.

claim: Flag-p107 expression led to a noticeable increase in the fraction of cells in G1.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Farkas et al., 2002), Flag-p107 expression led to a noticeable increase in the fraction of cells in G1 (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is based on cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 6E and supported by a citation to Farkas et al., 2002.

claim: The G1 arrest effect of Flag-p107 was drastically increased by coexpression of Myc-B55α.
source: Importantly, this effect was drastically increased by coexpression of Myc-B55α, which had a smaller effect on its own.
evidence: This is based on cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The effect of the Flag-p107 SLiM mutant in G1 was clearly diminished relatively to WT Flag-p107 even with co-transfected Myc-B55α.
source: The effect of the Flag-p107 SLiM mutant in G1 was clearly diminished relatively to WT Flag-p107 even with co-transfected Myc-B55α.
evidence: This is based on cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: B55α-mediated dephosphorylation of S615 in cells is dependent on specific residues C-terminal from the target dephosphorylation site that mediate contacts with B55α D197 and/or neighboring residues in B55α.
source: Altogether, these data strongly suggest that B55α-mediated dephosphorylation of S615 in cells is dependent on specific residues C-terminal from the target dephosphorylation site that mediate contacts with B55α D197 and/or neighboring residues in B55α
evidence: This is inferred from the cellular data showing SLiM-dependent dephosphorylation.

claim: The SLiM is critically important for modulation of the cell cycle suppressing function of p107.
source: and that the SLiM is critically important for modulation of the cell cycle suppressing function of p107.
evidence: This is inferred from the cell cycle analysis data showing reduced G1 arrest with the SLiM mutant.

claim: Cyclin E clearly reduces the p107-induced G1 arrest, and this effect is counteracted by Myc-B55α.
source: Cell cycle analyses showed that cyclin E clearly reduces the p107-induced G1 arrest, and this effect is counteracted by Myc-B55α (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is based on cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Co-transfection of Myc-B55α and/or cyclin E had little effect on the abundance of Flag-p107/HA-E2F4 complexes.
source: However, co-transfection of Myc-B55α and/or cyclin E had little effect on the abundance of Flag-p107/HA-E2F4 complexes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: B55α promotes p107 activation and cell cycle arrest at least in part by opposing cyclin E/CDK2 function likely by mechanisms independent of E2F4.
source: Altogether, it suggests that B55α promotes p107 activation and cell cycle arrest at least in part by opposing cyclin E/CDK2 function likely by mechanisms independent of E2F4.
evidence: This is inferred from the cell cycle and co-immunoprecipitation data.

claim: Shifts in E2F4 protein isoform migration with Myc-B55α co-transfection may indicate that E2F4 is also dephosphorylated, perhaps as a result of complex formation with p107.
source: Of note, we also observed shifts in E2F4 protein isoform migration with Myc-B55α co-transfection, which may indicate that E2F4 is also dephosphorylated, perhaps as a result of complex formation with p107.
evidence: This is based on observation of E2F4 migration shifts and speculation about the cause.

claim: The 520 identified peptides with the sequences xEPxxxPRx have distances between 15 and 25 Å.
source: The 520 identified peptides with the sequences xEPxxxPRx have distances between 15 and 25 Å (Figure 7—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is based on structural database analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: p107 pSPMLHPR must form a highly extended structure when bound to PP2A/B55.
source: indicating that p107 pSPMLHPR must form a highly extended structure when bound to PP2A/B55.
evidence: This is inferred from the distance analysis of peptide structures.

claim: In the best PP2A/B55α/p107 model, the NH2 side chain of R621p107 is 3.2 Å apart from D197B55α.
source: In the best PP2A/B55α/p107 model, the NH2 side chain of R621p107 is 3.2 Å apart from D197B55α
evidence: This is based on computational modeling data.

claim: In the best PP2A/B55α/p107 model, the OE1/OE2 of E615 (pS615 mimic) is 4.4 and 5.1 Å apart from the two Mn2+ ions at the PP2A active site, respectively.
source: while the OE1/OE2 of E615 (pS615 mimic) is 4.4 and 5.1 Å apart from the two Mn2+ ions at the PP2A active site, respectively (Figure 7C–E).
evidence: This is based on computational modeling data shown in Figure 7C-E.

claim: Replacing E615 with pS615 shows consistency with active site binding of PPPs.
source: These distances are slightly longer than expected for this type of interactions, but replacing E615 with pS615 shows consistency with active site binding of PPPs (Figure 7F; Goldberg et al., 1995).
evidence: This is based on computational modeling data shown in Figure 7F and supported by a citation to Goldberg et al., 1995.

claim: p107 pSPLMHPRV can bind in a highly extended fashion to the PP2A/B55α holoenzyme, in full agreement with experimental data.
source: Taken together, our model shows that p107 pSPLMHPRV can bind in a highly extended fashion to the PP2A/B55α holoenzyme, in full agreement with our experimental data.
evidence: This is inferred from the computational modeling data and its agreement with experimental data.

claim: TAU and MAP2 and the conserved p107 family member, p130, contain residues that align with the defined p107 SLiM.
source: We noticed that TAU and MAP2 and the conserved p107 family member, p130, contain residues that align with our defined p107 SLiM, generating a consensus sequence, p[ST]-P-x(4,10)-[RK]-V-x-x-[VI]-R (Figure 8A)
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The phosphosite is 5–10 residues amino terminal from the conserved residues in the binding motif.
source: and other cellular IDPs, where the phosphosite is 5–10 residues amino terminal from the conserved residues in the binding motif.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of substrates with the SLiM.

claim: Disruption of critical residues within the newly defined B55α substrate SLiM completely blocks TAU dephosphorylation.
source: Figure 8B shows that disruption of critical residues within the newly defined B55α substrate SLiM completely blocks TAU dephosphorylation.
evidence: This is based on Malachite Green Phosphatase Assay data with TAU peptides shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The fraction of proteins with the SLiM greatly increases among a dataset of B55α interactors and potential in vitro B55α mitotic substrates.
source: Figure 8—figure supplement 1 shows that the fraction of proteins with the SLiM greatly increases among a dataset of B55α interactors (Hertz et al., 2016) and potential in vitro B55α mitotic substrates (Kruse et al., 2020).
evidence: This is based on computational analysis of datasets shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1 and supported by citations to Hertz et al., 2016 and Kruse et al., 2020.

claim: This enrichment indicates that many substrates and B55 interactors potentially use this SLiM-based mechanism.
source: This enrichment indicates that many substrates and B55 interactors potentially use this SLiM-based mechanism.
evidence: This is inferred from the enrichment analysis.

claim: Sites of the acidic surface of B55α that were required for Tau dephosphorylation appeared dispensable for p107 binding.
source: Specifically, sites of the acidic surface of B55α that were required for Tau dephosphorylation (Xu et al., 2008) appeared dispensable for p107 binding (Jayadeva et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Xu et al., 2008 and Jayadeva et al., 2010.

claim: p107 S615 (CDK kinase phosphorylation site) is a specific B55α/PP2A holoenzyme dephosphorylation site.
source: We show that p107 S615 (CDK kinase phosphorylation site) is a specific B55α/PP2A holoenzyme dephosphorylation site.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from in vitro and cellular assays.

claim: p107 residues H619, R621, V622, and V625 within the pSPxxxHxRVxxV motif are critical for binding to B55α in vitro and in cells.
source: p107 residues H619, R621, V622, and V625 within the pSPxxxHxRVxxV motif are critical for binding to B55α in vitro and in cells.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from binding and cellular assays.

claim: These residues bind to a B55α surface groove that is defined by residues D197 and L225.
source: Next, we showed that these residues bind to a B55α surface groove that is defined by residues D197 and L225.
evidence: This is based on mutagenesis data of B55α residues.

claim: This B55α surface is also important for recruitment of pRB and KSR.
source: Importantly, our results show that this B55α surface is also important for recruitment of pRB and KSR, further suggesting that these sites are likely the key substrate recruitment sites for a variety of substrates.
evidence: This is based on mutagenesis data showing that D197 and L225 are important for multiple substrates.

claim: pRB and KSR differ in the requirement of other conserved residues present within the B55α groove.
source: However, pRB and KSR differ in the requirement of other conserved residues present within the B55α groove, strongly suggesting that while substrate specificity is determined by the groove, it may use different residues to accommodate a variety of substrates.
evidence: This is based on mutagenesis data showing different B55α residues are required for different substrates.

claim: Peptides known to abrogate Tau and MAP2 binding to B55α contain residues that align with the proposed SLiM consensus sequence.
source: With this regard, we have found that peptides known to abrogate Tau and MAP2 binding to B55α (Sontag et al., 2012) contain residues that align with our proposed SLiM consensus sequence, p[ST]-P-x(4,10)-[RK]-V-x-x-[VI]-R
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment analysis and supported by a citation to Sontag et al., 2012.

claim: The number of residues between the conserved residues that contact the groove and the phosphorylation site varies but can be very small (5 residues in p107 vs. 7 residues in TAU and 11 in MAP2).
source: It appears that the number of residues between the conserved residues that contact the groove and the phosphorylation site varies but can be very small (5 residues in p107 vs. 7 residues in TAU and 11 in MAP2), which suggests a role for the SLiM in phosphosite presentation.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and speculation about the role of the SLiM.

claim: Recent work on the B56 SLiM suggests that B56 SLiM-containing proteins are direct substrates as well as scaffolds to facilitate the recruitment of proteins to B56/PP2A for dephosphorylation.
source: In contrast, recent work on the B56 SLiM suggests that B56 SLiM-containing proteins are direct substrates as well as scaffolds to facilitate the recruitment of proteins to B56/PP2A for dephosphorylation (Kruse et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kruse et al., 2020.

claim: There is some correlation between the distance of the B56 SLiM and the site of dephosphorylation and the rate of dephosphorylation.
source: While there is some correlation between the distance of the B56 SLiM and the site of dephosphorylation and the rate of dephosphorylation
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about B56.

claim: Many B56-dependent phosphorylation sites are located on non-SLIM-containing proteins indicating B regulatory subunit-specific dephosphorylation mechanisms.
source: many B56-dependent phosphorylation sites are located on non-SLIM-containing proteins indicating B regulatory subunit-specific dephosphorylation mechanisms.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about B56.

claim: A second region of p107, termed R2, contributes to B55α binding.
source: Moreover, we also identified a second region of p107, which we termed R2, that contributes to B55α binding.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from binding assays.

claim: The R2 region includes a higher density of positively charged residues that enhance binding most likely via charged:charged interactions (R647, and K657 and/or R659).
source: This R2 region includes a higher density of positively charged residues that enhance binding most likely via charged:charged interactions (R647, and K657 and/or R659).
evidence: This is based on mutagenesis data and speculation about the mechanism.

claim: Dynamic charged:charged interactions have been recently shown to play a role in substrate specificity for protein phosphatase 2B (PP2B; PP3; calcineurin) and the B56 regulatory subunit of PP2A.
source: Indeed, this has also been recently shown for protein phosphatase 2B (PP2B; PP3; calcineurin) and the B56 regulatory subunit of PP2A, where these dynamic charged:charged interactions were shown to play a role in substrate specificity (Hendus-Altenburger et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Hendus-Altenburger et al., 2019 and Wang et al., 2020.

claim: Such charged:charged interactions are likely important for substrate recruitment and specificity by different phosphatases.
source: Thus, such interactions, which have been recently recognized to be critical for the interaction of IDPs with their target proteins and allow for increased entropy, are likely important for substrate recruitment and specificity by different phosphatases.
evidence: This is inferred from the data on charged:charged interactions and their role in IDP interactions.

claim: The computational model shows the feasibility of simultaneous binding of both the active site of PP2A/C and D197 on the B55α groove.
source: Our computational model based on structural data of peptides with the conserved key residues on p107 needed for B55α binding shows the feasibility of simultaneous binding of both the active site of PP2A/C and D197 on the B55α groove.
evidence: This is based on computational modeling data.

claim: The model peptide is significantly extended, a conformation that would not be favored for catalysis without additional bending of the scaffold subunit.
source: However, the model peptide is significantly extended, a conformation that would not be favored for catalysis without additional bending of the scaffold subunit.
evidence: This is based on computational modeling data and speculation about catalysis.

claim: Analysis of the flexibility of the PP2A/A scaffold upon binding to the catalytic subunit, and B subunits of the four distinct holoenzymes, confirms that subunit binding has a major effect on PP2A/A bending.
source: Analysis of the flexibility of the PP2A/A scaffold upon binding to the catalytic subunit, and B subunits of the four distinct holoenzymes, confirms that subunit binding has a major effect on PP2A/A bending (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The dependency of the conformational flexibility of the scaffold subunit on the nature of the B subunit bound strongly suggests that substrate binding should result in additional relative movement of PP2A/A HEAT-repeats to promote catalysis.
source: The dependency of the conformational flexibility of the scaffold subunit on the nature of the B subunit bound strongly suggests that substrate binding should result in additional relative movement of PP2A/A HEAT-repeats to promote catalysis.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis and speculation about the mechanism.
